notes: 0.1.0a5 is a publication-recovery release. It carries the 0.1.0a4 implementation unchanged and fixes the release system that published one of fourteen artifacts. ADR 0078 records why the alpha line gained it and why Execution Semantics moved to 0.1.0a6.

0.1.0a4 was partially published on 2026-09-08. Workflow run 34285830444 uploaded agnara-0.1.0a4-py3-none-any.whl (HTTP 200) and was rejected on agnara_a2a-0.1.0a4-py3-none-any.whl with HTTP 400 'Non-user identities cannot create new projects'. Twine uploads wheels before sdists and stops on the first failure, so the agnara 0.1.0a4 sdist and all twelve sibling artifacts were never uploaded, post-release verification never ran, and no GitHub Release was created. v0.1.0a4 remains historical and unmodified.

The gate that was missing is now explicit. publication-prerequisites re-derives PUBLISH READY from the repository on every run, and pypi-trusted-publishers is a manual gate the tooling can never satisfy. docs/releases/publication.json is the reviewed record of the external registry configuration; it is UNVERIFIED until the owner reads the tuples back from PyPI.
Status is recomputed by scripts/check_release_readiness.py; automated outcomes are never trusted from this file.

gates.title: Python 3.14 baseline verified
Changelog accurately describes changes since 0.1.0a3
Version references are internally consistent
Working tree is clean at the release commit
The release commit is identified
LICENSE present and every package declares Apache-2.0
Every distributable package declares its public surface
The reviewed publication set is publishable, not merely buildable
Full supported test suite passes
Package build succeeds
Clean-environment installation smoke test succeeds
HTTP integration tests pass
MCP integration and conformance tests pass
CLI smoke tests pass
No known release-blocking regression
Public documentation reflects the implementation
gates.detail: Whether the documentation 0.1.0a4 actually ships matches the implementation is a maintainer judgment, not a test result. The owner accepted it on the corrected MCP, CLI and lifecycle guidance, whose examples tests/docs executes. Alpha APIs may still change without a deprecation cycle.

gates.title: Security and release checks required by QUALITY_GATES.md
gates.detail: Whether the experimental-alpha security posture satisfies QUALITY_GATES.md is the owner's decision. The basis: 29 locked runtime dependencies audited with pip-audit 2.10.1 and zero known vulnerabilities, 38 security tests, native secret scanning and push protection enabled, and required Python and Actions CodeQL completed. The three pre-existing develop findings are dispositioned in v0.1.0a4.md rather than reported as a zero-alert result. Non-provider patterns and validity checks remain disabled, and the pypi environment protection policy remains an owner choice.

gates.title: Reference applications exist and install Agnara as an ordinary dependency
No reference application imports Agnara internals
No reference application requires a monkey patch
Public APIs are sufficient to build the reference applications
gates.detail: Whether the governed public surface is sufficient to build the reference applications is a maintainer judgment. The external consumer used governed names for every implemented adapter across 282 exports in 47 public modules. A2A and events intentionally expose no runtime in a4.

gates.title: Dependency injection works naturally from an application
gates.detail: Whether dependency injection works naturally from outside the framework is a maintainer judgment. The external application resolved and cleaned up singletons without a workaround, and HTTP now closes the resources it owns on lifespan shutdown for both sync and async providers. A container belongs to one event loop.

gates.title: Capabilities can be declared cleanly from an application
gates.detail: Whether capability declaration is clean enough to ship is a maintainer judgment. The external application declared and compiled capabilities with ordinary decorators and explicit compilation, with no monkey patch and no private import.

gates.title: HTTP exposure works from an application
MCP exposure works from an application, where applicable
Schemas stay coherent across transports
Policies behave consistently across transports
Failures stay structured across transports
CLI and introspection materially help a developer
gates.detail: Whether the CLI and introspection materially help a developer is a maintainer judgment. The installed console script answered inspect, graph, context and schema openapi, plus help, version and dry-run scaffolding, from outside the checkout. Importing a target executes trusted application code.

gates.title: Documentation is sufficient to reproduce the applications
gates.detail: Whether the public documentation alone is enough to reproduce the applications is an explicit maintainer judgment. The clean-room consumer was built from public consumer guides without source inspection, and the migration guide describes the new shutdown behaviour.

gates.title: Every framework deficiency found by dogfooding is tracked
Baseline benchmarks published
The release pipeline cannot report success on a partial publication
The 0.1.0a4 partial publication is recorded truthfully and not rewritten
Every PyPI Trusted Publisher is confirmed for this exact target
gates.detail: Only the repository owner can read a Trusted Publisher tuple back from PyPI. No repository check can observe it, and 0.1.0a4 shipped on the assumption that it had been done. Confirmation is recorded per project in docs/releases/publication.json and must name the target it was made for.
